# Behavioral Specification: Parameterized Subregister

## Overview

This primitive implements one parameterized-width storage element with configurable software and/or hardware update behavior. It provides the current stored value, a software-visible read value, a write strobe, and the next value to be stored.

The access behavior is selected by an access-type parameter. All storage is reset to a programmable reset value.

## Parameters

- **Width**: The storage element is N bits wide.
- **Access type**: Selects the update semantics for software and/or hardware writes.
- **Reset value**: The value loaded into the storage element on reset. If not otherwise specified, this value shall be all zeros.

## Reset and Clocking

- The storage element shall initialize to the reset value when reset is asserted.
- Reset is asynchronous and active-low.
- All non-reset updates shall be captured on the rising edge of the clock.
- If no write is accepted in a cycle, the storage element shall retain its current value.

## Value Outputs

- **Current stored value**: This output shall reflect the actual value held in the storage element.
- **Software-visible value**: This output shall present the value used for software read data. Except for the read-to-clear special case described below, it shall equal the current stored value.
- **Next-state value**: This output shall show the value that will be captured on the next rising edge if a write is accepted. If no write is accepted, it shall follow the software-visible value.
- **Write strobe**: This output shall be asserted in a cycle in which the storage element is written by an active write source. It indicates an accepted write operation, not necessarily a change in the stored value.

## Access Modes

The following behavior shall apply for each access type:

| Access mode | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only | Software writes are ignored. When hardware write enable `de` is asserted, the storage element updates to hardware data `d`. |
| Read-write | A software write request shall store the supplied software write data. |
| Write-only | A software write request shall store the supplied software write data. Software read access is not defined for this mode. |
| Write-1-to-clear | On a software write request, each bit for which the write-data bit is 1 shall be cleared to 0. Bits for which the write-data bit is 0 shall remain unchanged. |
| Write-1-to-set | On a software write request, each bit for which the write-data bit is 1 shall be set to 1. Bits for which the write-data bit is 0 shall remain unchanged. |
| Write-0-to-clear | On a software write request, each bit for which the write-data bit is 0 shall be cleared to 0. Bits for which the write-data bit is 1 shall remain unchanged. |
| Read-to-clear | A software read request shall return the current stored value through the software-visible output and shall clear the storage element to 0 on the clock edge. A hardware write request shall update the storage element to the supplied hardware write data. If a software read request and a hardware write request occur in the same cycle, the software-visible output shall be the hardware write data, but the storage element shall be cleared to 0. |
| Hardware read-write / hardware write-only | A hardware write request shall update the storage element to the supplied hardware write data. Software write requests shall be ignored. |

## Write Source Requirements

- A write source that is not active for the selected access mode shall have no effect on the stored value or on the write strobe.
- For modes with bit-wise side effects, each bit shall behave independently of the other bits.
- The write strobe shall be asserted for any accepted write from an active write source. In read-to-clear mode, a read request that clears the storage element shall also assert the write strobe.
